info.bio:
Norman Greenbaum (nacido el 20 de noviembre de 1942 en Malden, Massachusetts, EE.UU.) es un cantautor estadounidense. Estudió música en la Boston University.

scenes.name: Carreras en solitario: cantautores de finales de los sesenta
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Los excéntricos de Los Ángeles (David Axelrod, cuyos breakbeats orquestales anticipan el trip-hop; Van Dyke Parks y su música de cámara pop; David Ackles, Kim Fowley, Wild Man Fischer) y los herederos del Greenwich (Laura Nyro, Eric Andersen, David Peel, Angus MacLise y Nico, cuyas letanías fúnebres inventan el rock gótico casi por accidente: Marble Index, Desert Shore). Canadá aporta a Leonard Cohen, Gordon Lightfoot, Joni Mitchell (Blue, Hejira) y Neil Young, que con Dylan y Springsteen forma la gran tríada «moral» de la música americana e inventa la guitarra distorsionada que influirá en el grunge. En Texas, Townes Van Zandt; en Gran Bretaña, Scott Walker, Nick Drake (Pink Moon), Roy Harper, John Martyn, Cat Stevens, Rod Stewart, Eric Burdon y Jack Bruce.

podcast.title: Inspiration from Country Gospel
podcast.body: Norman Greenbaum, despite being Jewish, was inspired to write "Spirit in the Sky" by a country gospel song, "Pastor Absent on Vacation," performed by Porter Wagoner. This shows the cross-genre influence of religious themes. "Norman Greenbaum, yes, he is Jewish, was inspired to write Spirit in the Sky by hearing Country Star Porter Wagner sing Pastor Absent on vacation on television."

podcast.title: Reception and Intent of "Spirit in the Sky"
podcast.body: Some listeners were unhappy with the lyric "never been a sinner, never sinned," perceiving it as making light of religious beliefs. Greenbaum clarified 50 years later that he "met no harm" and didn't intend it as a joke or against anyone, simply that "It wasn't my religion, I just did it." He noted that many churches later incorporated the song into their services. "It did upset some people. When I said I can do this, that didn't mean I could do it perfectly."
